scenarios.title: Repair a Linux interface without disturbing management
scenarios.summary: Investigate link state and address/prefix separately, then verify the supplied LAN.
scenarios.objective: Bring ens3 up and configure one unused conventional host address in 192.0.2.0/24. Do not use network/broadcast or any supplied peer/gateway address. Provide usable virtual LAN paths to 192.0.2.20 and 192.0.2.200 through ens3. Keep ens4’s complete management interface state and the 10.40.0.0/24 route unchanged.
steps: Inspect the supplied host, repair the complete assignment and verify every required path while retaining protected state.
scenarios.explanation: One valid approach: ip -4 address del 10.20.0.10/24 dev ens3; ip -4 address add 192.0.2.10/24 dev ens3; ip link set dev ens3 up. Inspect actual state after the changes and check every required outcome. Other unused host addresses, valid route repairs and supported resolver formatting can pass; this is not an exact-command-string grade.
hints: Separate administrative link state, address/prefix, route choice and resolver configuration. Inspect each before changing healthy settings.
A longer prefix wins before metric. A native virtual path test and a supplied DNS answer prove different things.
Preserve the stated management interface/routes and save resolver drafts before checking all outcomes.
scenarios.simplifications: Bounded IPv4 host model only: one primary per supplied interface, simplified main-table unicast gateway routes and supplied path/DNS facts. No real kernel, ARP, packets, RTTs, DHCP, IPv6, policy routing, namespaces, full NSS, NetworkManager or Linux boot persistence. Unsupported command forms fail explicitly. Virtual resolver editor never reads/writes host files.

example_actions.input: ip link set dev ens3 up

solution: host-action {"kind":"Command","input":"ip link set dev ens3 up"}

Keep both interface configurations and every 10.40.0.0/24 management route entry unchanged.

scenarios.title: Hand over application networking while preserving management
scenarios.summary: Combine interface, route and resolver repair without disturbing the separate management path.
scenarios.objective: Repair ens3 with one unused conventional 192.0.2.0/24 address and bring it up. Make the preferred default use 192.0.2.1 on ens3. Provide virtual application paths to 203.0.113.80 and 203.0.113.90 through ens3; resolve service.lab.test and inventory.lab.test to those respective addresses. Retain ens4’s complete management state and every 10.40.0.0/24 route entry. The management path to 10.40.0.20 must still use ens4. Save any virtual resolver changes before checking. Valid address/metric choices are accepted when all required outcomes hold.
steps: Inspect the supplied host, repair the complete assignment and verify every required path while retaining protected state.

Inspect actual state after the changes and check every required outcome. Other unused host addresses, valid route repairs and supported resolver formatting can pass; this is not an exact-command-string grade.
